Apple___Apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease of apples that causes dark, scabby lesions on leaves and fruit. It is favored by cool, wet weather in the spring.
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Use disease-resistant varieties. Apply fungicides preventatively starting at green tip and continuing until the fruit is well formed. Remove fallen leaves in autumn.

Apple___Black_rot.name: Apple Black Rot
Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease causing frog-eye leaf spot, fruit rot, and cankers on branches. Infection often occurs through wounds.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune out and destroy infected branches and cankers. Remove mummified fruit. Apply appropriate fungicides from silver tip to harvest.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.name: Cedar Apple Rust
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease that requires both apple and juniper (cedar) plants to complete its life cycle. It causes yellow-orange spots on apple leaves.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Remove nearby cedar trees if possible. Apply preventative fungicides to apple trees from pink bud to shortly after petal fall.

Apple___healthy.name: Healthy Apple
Apple___healthy.description: The leaf appears healthy with no visible signs of fungal or bacterial diseases.
Apple___healthy.treatment: Continue regular maintenance, adequate watering, and routine fertilization to keep the plant healthy.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal disease affecting corn that produces rectangular, gray to brown lesions on the leaves, which can merge and blight the entire leaf.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Plant resistant hybrids. Implement crop rotation (do not plant corn in the same field consecutively). Use tillage to help decompose crop residue, and apply fungicides if needed.
